newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani president recovering from illness.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani president recovering from illness.

text.p: Pakistani President Farooq Leghari, who sacked Benazir Bhutto's government last week, was recovering on Monday after being taken ill, apparently with kidney trouble, his spokesman said.
He said Leghari had not gone to his office for the past two days and had been taken to hospital for tests on Sunday night.
"They asked him to stay there in case they needed to do more tests, but he refused and returned home," he said.
The spokesman said Leghari, 56, had received the provincial governors of North West Frontier Province and Punjab on Monday and would meet caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid on Tuesday.
He said Leghari's sudden illness may have been triggered by a vigorous exercise session, combined with strain and sleepless nights since he dismissed Bhutto's government last Tuesday.
Information and Broadcasting Minister Irshad Ahmed Haqqani told a news conference that Leghari's condition had improved.
"His condition is much better than before," he said, but gave no details. "I am not a doctor and the tests have not been shown to me," Haqqani added.
"He was not feeling well from Saturday evening," an official at the president's palace said earlier.
"He had a pain in his kidney on Sunday morning and was given pain-killing injections. Probably his pain got severe after which he went to the hospital for immediate treatment and tests," he said.

Leghari was rushed to the Combined Military Hospital in Rawalpindi, near Islamabad, at about midnight for tests that included a chest X-ray, an electrocardiogram and an ultrasound scan of his abdomen, staff there said.
"He was normal," said one staffer, who did not elaborate.

The president, who will complete his third year in office on Wednesday, moved to the centre of Pakistan's political stage last Tuesday when he abruptly dismissed Bhutto's government, dissolved parliament and appointed a caretaker premier to guide the turbulent country into an election set for February 3.
